proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 1, printed proof of Theorem 4.16 (p. 37): "By the Alaoglu theorem there is a subsequence F_{j,k'} and a non-negative bounded functional F_j : C(K_j) → ℝ with F_{j,k'}(f) → F_j(f) for each f ∈ C(K_j). By choosing the subsequences successively and taking a diagonal sequence, we then get a subsequence μ_{k'} and a non-negative linear F : K(X) → ℝ with ∫_X f dμ_{k'} → F(f) for each f ∈ K(X)". ERRATUM (GMT/Ch01/README.md; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_16_counterexample): as printed (X only locally compact, σ-compact, Hausdorff) this is false, because the Alaoglu step yields a subnet and not a subsequence; for second-countable X the step is made sequential exactly as in steps 3–4 of the parent proof: extract a diagonal subsequence along a countable family of test functions (the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx) and extend to all test functions by uniform approximation and the local mass bounds. Second (immaterial) adaptation, as in the parent: the mass bounds are only assumed for all sufficiently large j (finitely many μ_j may have infinite mass on K). This lemma is steps 3–4 of the parent proof of varifold_radon_compactness, for a general locally compact, Hausdorff, second-countable X with its Borel σ-algebra.

Notation. For a measure ν and f : X → ℝ, ∫ f dν is the Bochner integral (it is 0 by convention when f is not ν-integrable; every estimate below is used only for indices at which integrability has been verified, or is valid without integrability). For a compact (hence closed, hence Borel) set K and a measure ν with ν(K) < ∞ write ν(K) also for the real number (ν K).toReal.

0. Two elementary facts.
 (a) Integrability. Let h ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), K ⊆ X a compact set with tsupport h ⊆ K, and ν a measure on X with ν(K) < ∞. Then h is ν-integrable. Indeed h is continuous, hence (X Borel, ℝ second countable) a.e.-strongly measurable for ν; h is bounded, |h(x)| ≤ M for all x, since it is continuous with compact support (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support); so h is integrable on K (a bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure; Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), and since h = 0 outside K (support h ⊆ tsupport h ⊆ K) it is integrable on X (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).
 (b) Estimate. Let K ⊆ X be compact, ν a measure with ν(K) < ∞, η ≥ 0 a real number and h : X → ℝ with h(x) = 0 for x ∉ K and |h(x)| ≤ η for all x. Then |∫ h dν| ≤ η ν(K). Indeed ∫ h dν = ∫_K h dν because h vanishes off K (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and |∫_K h dν| ≤ η ν(K) (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).

1. The countable family. By the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx (X is locally compact, Hausdorff, second countable) there is a sequence (g_k)_{k∈ℕ} in C_c(X,ℝ) such that for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) there is a compact K_f ⊆ X with tsupport f ⊆ K_f and, for every η > 0, some k with tsupport g_k ⊆ K_f and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x ∈ X.

2. Each sequence a_k(j) := ∫ g_k dμ_j (j ∈ ℕ) is bounded. Fix k and let T_k := tsupport g_k, a compact set. By hypothesis there are C_k ∈ [0,∞) and J_k ∈ ℕ with μ_j(T_k) ≤ C_k for all j ≥ J_k; write c_k := C_k as a real number (c_k ≥ 0). Choose M_k ∈ ℝ with |g_k(x)| ≤ M_k for all x (0(a)); then also |g_k(x)| ≤ |M_k|. For j ≥ J_k we have μ_j(T_k) ≤ C_k < ∞, so by 0(b) (with h = g_k, K = T_k, η = |M_k|) |a_k(j)| ≤ |M_k| μ_j(T_k) ≤ |M_k| c_k. Put B_k := |M_k| c_k + Σ_{j < J_k} |a_k(j)|. Then |a_k(j)| ≤ B_k for every j ∈ ℕ: if j ≥ J_k this follows from the previous estimate because the finite sum is ≥ 0; if j < J_k, then |a_k(j)| is one of the nonnegative summands of Σ_{j' < J_k} |a_k(j')| and |M_k| c_k ≥ 0.

3. Diagonal extraction (the sequential form of "choosing the subsequences successively and taking a diagonal sequence"). Consider the space ℝ^ℕ of real sequences with the product topology and its points A_j := (a_k(j))_{k∈ℕ}, j ∈ ℕ. By step 2 every A_j lies in P := ∏_{k∈ℕ} [−B_k, B_k], which is compact by Tychonoff's theorem (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi with isCompact_Icc). The space ℝ^ℕ is first countable (a countable product of first-countable spaces; it is even metrizable), so the compact set P is sequentially compact (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq): there are a = (a_k)_k ∈ P and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with A_{φ(j)} → a in ℝ^ℕ as j → ∞. Convergence in the product topology is coordinatewise convergence (tendsto_pi_nhds), so for every k: ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(j)} = a_k(φ(j)) → a_k as j → ∞. In particular every sequence (a_k(φ(j)))_j is a Cauchy sequence.

4. Convergence for every test function. Let f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), and let K := K_f be the compact set of step 1, so tsupport f ⊆ K. By hypothesis there are C ∈ [0,∞) and J ∈ ℕ with μ_j(K) ≤ C for all j ≥ J; let c := C as a real number, c ≥ 0. We prove that (∫ f dμ_{φ(j)})_{j∈ℕ} is a Cauchy sequence of reals. Let ε > 0 and put η := ε/(2c + 2) > 0, so that η(2c + 2) = ε. By step 1 choose k with tsupport g_k ⊆ K and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x. By step 3 choose N_1 with |a_k(φ(p)) − a_k(φ(q))| < η for all p, q ≥ N_1.
 (i) For every p ≥ J: since φ is strictly increasing, φ(p) ≥ p ≥ J, so μ_{φ(p)}(K) ≤ C < ∞. By 0(a), f and g_k are μ_{φ(p)}-integrable (both have topological support in K), hence ∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(p)} = ∫ (f − g_k) dμ_{φ(p)}. The function f − g_k vanishes outside K (both f and g_k vanish outside their topological supports, which lie in K) and |f − g_k| ≤ η, so by 0(b) |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − a_k(φ(p))| ≤ η μ_{φ(p)}(K) ≤ η c.
 (ii) For p, q ≥ N := max(N_1, J), by the triangle inequality and (i),
 |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − ∫ f dμ_{φ(q)}| ≤ |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − a_k(φ(p))| + |a_k(φ(p)) − a_k(φ(q))| + |a_k(φ(q)) − ∫ f dμ_{φ(q)}| < ηc + η + ηc ≤ η(2c + 2) = ε.
 Hence the sequence is Cauchy (Metric.cauchySeq_iff), and since ℝ is complete it converges to some L ∈ ℝ (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete).
Since φ was chosen in step 3 independently of f, the strictly increasing φ works for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) simultaneously, which is the claim. ∎
key_steps: Countable approximating family g_k from the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx.
Each sequence (∫ g_k dμ_j)_j is bounded: eventual bound |M_k|·C_k plus the finitely many initial terms.
Tychonoff: ∏_k [−B_k, B_k] ⊆ ℝ^ℕ is compact and ℝ^ℕ is first countable, so a subsequence φ makes every ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(j)} converge (diagonal step).
For f ∈ C_c(X): approximate uniformly by g_k supported in K_f, use the eventual mass bound on K_f and φ(p) ≥ p to get a Cauchy sequence, hence a limit in ℝ.
